transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Kim (Redwood); Sam Rodriguez, Priya Singh, Ethan Lopez (Apex)

Summary (auto): POC scoping focusing on success criteria, workload sizing, and a 6-week POC timeline. Agreed to run benchmarks on Redwood hosted + dedicated variants, measure p95 latency and cost, and report mid-point findings to execs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, i'm maya from redwood inference, joined by jordan our se. how's it going sam?
[00:12] Sam: good thanks, busy quarter but excited to get this scoped, we want to validate performance for our routing engine and document costs before committing to a dedicated pool.
[00:22] Jordan: great, so agenda: success criteria, workload profile, benchmark plan, timeline and access. we'll propose kickoff next week and a 6-week POC with four milestones.
[00:34] Priya: yes, high level success criteria for us are p95 latency under 250ms for the 99th percentile small requests, end-to-end throughput to handle 50 rps with bursts to 200 for short windows, and an operational cost target under $X per 1M tokens - we can share exact number in doc. also data residency and SOC2 are musts.
[00:58] Maya: makes sense. to clarify p95 under 250ms - is that token-generation time or full request including network/transform?
[01:06] Priya: full request, from our edge to response. we can rework to separate network time but initial acceptance should include network.
[01:16] Jordan: ok we'll measure both client-to-redwood and token-gen only. for benchmarks we recommend running: 1) a synthetic closed-loop test to get raw token latency, 2) an injection test with 7-day trace replay to surface batched behavior and cache hit patterns, and 3) a production-like load test to capture p95 under burst.
[01:40] Sam: how do you handle caching? we have a lot of repeated prefixes across shipments.
[01:45] Jordan: we use prefix/KV cache and intelligent batching; note sometimes the transcript here says KV cash because auto-gen. but it's KV cache - it helps a lot for repeated prefixes, reduces token compute. we'll include quantization and model variant suggestions; hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs are mostly on cost predictability and isolation.
[02:08] Priya: we have a preference for dedicated if unit economics work, but we need to see the numbers. also on private/VPC we may need peering for PII lanes. do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:20] Maya: yes, KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated with customer-managed keys for enterprise plans; Hosted has envelope encryption by default and we can discuss bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. we'll attach the KMS note in the security pack.
[02:34] Ethan: firewall and peering - what's the minimal access for a POC? we want to avoid opening too much.
[02:40] Jordan: typical POC flow: 1) set up a read-only service account and ingress egress rules for the test runner, 2) if you want VPC peering we do that, else temporary IP allowlist. the benchmark harness runs from a small runner that we can host or you can run internally. we'll document steps.
[03:00] Sam: timeline? you mentioned 6 weeks earlier, can you break that down?
[03:05] Maya: sure, proposed milestones: Week 0: kickoff and access setup; Week 1-2: baseline benchmarks and raw token latency tests (hosted variant); Week 3: mid-point review with findings and recommended config (quantization/model variant, batching settings); Week 4-5: run dedicated variant and production-like load tests; Week 6: exec readout with results and recommended next steps (pilot or reserved capacity).
[03:36] Priya: mid-point review — will that include concrete perf numbers and cost estimates?
[03:40] Jordan: yes, mid-point will include p50/p95/p99, token cost estimates per 1M tokens, and recommended configuration for production including batching, cache hit expectations, and autoscaling policy suggestions.
[03:55] Sam: for workloads sizing, we can provide you with a 7-day traffic trace and a sample of 10k requests representing our heavy tails. will that be enough?
[04:05] Jordan: that's ideal. the trace should include request size distribution, sequence length histograms, and any rate-limiting patterns. that lets us calibrate batching windows and the kernel selection model.
[04:20] Priya: any limitations on model variants? we plan to test an open model you recommended - redwood/opt-xx maybe?
[04:28] Jordan: we can test the curated open models in our catalog plus a few Redwood-verified variants; if you have a licensed model we can also run private model inference in Dedicated/Private. slight transcription note: sometimes model names get munged in auto text.
[04:40] Maya: security: we'll share SOC2 report, network diagram, and our data handling policy. we also have audit logs and RBAC in the console. does Apex need SAML SSO for the exec readout access?
[04:54] Sam: not for the readout, but for long-term pilots yes. we use Okta SSO.
[05:00] Jordan: we support SAML/Okta for Dedicated/Private; for POC we typically use invite links and then add SSO once you're ready.
[05:10] Priya: benchmarks - how do you measure cost per token? is it simulated or actual run?
[05:16] Jordan: we'll run the tests on hosted and dedicated setups and calculate actual compute consumption and token counts, then apply pricing to produce a $/1M tokens figure. we'll include sensitivity to batching and cache hit rate.
[05:28] Ethan: any red flags in our ask? our peak bursts to 200 rps are short but frequent during batch windows.
[05:36] Jordan: bursts are fine, we can configure autoscale and burst capacity in Dedicated; with Hosted we rely on multi-tenant elastic capacity but we'll show observed tail latency during bursts in the benchmark results.
[05:50] Maya: next, logistics: kickoff next Tues 2026-11-10, maya will propose 2 times. prior to kickoff we need sample traces, a contact for firewall setup, and the SSO admin if you want SAML enabled later.
[06:05] Sam: i'll get those over, priya will own dataset and ethan firewall.
[06:10] Priya: yep.
[06:12] Maya: ok recap: Redwood will send security pack and pricing by 11-04, SE to send benchmark plan by 11-06, customer to deliver traces and infra contacts by 11-05, and kickoff week of 11-10. mid-point review target week 3 of the POC, exec readout week 6. any other questions?
[06:32] Sam: just one on success criteria thresholds - can we formalize acceptance tests? like p95 < 250ms for 90% of test windows and cost within +/- 20% of target?
[06:44] Jordan: yes we'll put acceptance tests in the benchmark doc — p95 latency slice, throughput targets, and cost band for go/no-go.
[06:52] Priya: and we'll get legal looped in if the security pack looks good.
[06:58] Maya: perfect, i'll send the notes and action items. thanks everyone.
[07:02] Sam: thanks, talk soon.

Auto notes: References mentioned - security pack, benchmark plan, sample traces. Action items captured above. Transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors and name mis-attributions typical of call exports.
